answer: Cross-Epoch Drift Scoring. Each identity's action distribution is scored against its own prior-epoch profile using a similarity metric; new identities get an untrusted baseline. A mesa-like plateau of stable behaviour earns weight, while sudden shifts trigger a fable test: the agent must replay prior-epoch tasks and match its stored outputs. Aggregated over a spiral of epochs, drift beyond threshold freezes economic rights until consistency is restored. Sybils pay by sustaining parallel, costly behavioural histories across many epochs before each fake identity earns any weight.
